parts.text: Which claim correctly describes the angle they form?

options.text: The rays share starting point $Q$ (the vertex); the arms are $QR$ and $QS$; the angle may be named $\angle RQS$.
The vertex of the angle is arm $QR$.
Ray $QR$ and ray $QS$ form this angle even if they start at two different points.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Nisha draws two rays from a common point $Q$ on her chalkboard: ray $QR$ and ray $QS$.

part_answers.answer: An angle needs two rays with a common starting point; that common point $Q$ is the vertex, the rays are the arms, and the three-letter name $\angle RQS$ places the vertex letter in the middle.

teacher.key_rationale: Two rays from Q form an angle with vertex Q and arms QR, QS; name ∠RQS. B swaps vertex for an arm. C drops the shared-start condition.
